checks: Matched e917eba155dec2d6 §1 (1)–(3). Positivity of the three off-diagonal entries yields strictly positive determinant, while zero trace excludes three positive eigenvalues. Symmetry then gives one positive and two negative eigenvalues, so for r>0 the determinant of rI−B has the sign of r−J.

Expanding the cubic yields M^3 det(rI−B)=rM(r²M²−kT)−2k^(3/2)√U. Since U>0, the zero determinant needs strictly positive E_r. Squaring preserves the sign comparison exactly on the nonnegative E_r branch. This proves both strict and nonstrict tests.

Translate the fixed interior mark to zero. On a strict-incidence interval each edge-line intersection has rational coordinates in the parameter. Shoelace gives rational area; the signed difference projected onto a fixed perpendicular to v, divided by |v|², gives the normalized chord up to a fixed sign. Nondegeneracy keeps the sign fixed. Positive known denominator signs allow polynomial tests. Continuity of the symmetric largest eigenvalue proves the crossing statement.

overlap.comparison: Uses the characteristic determinant and the signed radical test at three rational parameter points on one fixed diagonal and one chosen level. The present criterion applies to arbitrary positive data and all r>0, and includes the fixed-incidence rationality and continuous crossing statement.
Uses the same determinant sign at level one in an actual planar sector optimization; it does not state the arbitrary-level two-polynomial test on positive data or the moving-vertex conclusion.

readability: Rationality is in the path parameter with the fixed geometry giving the coefficients. Translating the fixed mark to the origin is implicit in the clipping equation.
